To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the semiclassical magnetotunneling theory of the quantum well in a tilt field is based on short periodic orbit contributions, which are in turn determined by the bifurcation structure of traversing periodic orbits, and that the theory reproduces all features of the experimental resonance spectrum.

(i) the magnetotunnel current is determined by the stability of periodic orbits in the quantum well, (ii) the stability of these orbits depends crucially on the energy of the electron, (iii) there are energy bands where the periodic orbits are stable and bands where they are unstable, (iv) the energy bands are very narrow and are not easily resolved in the experiments, and (v) in spite of these difficulties, the semiclassical theory is in excellent agreement with the experiments.

(1) the magnetotunnel resonance spectrum of a quantum well in tilted field is dominated by the periodic orbits of the underlying classical dynamics and (2) these periodic orbits are related to bifurcation of the period-one orbits and exist only in finite energy intervals.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the semiclassical theory of the quantum tunneling resonance spectrum of a quantum well in an applied magnetic field.
the study of quantum mechanical tunneling through a quantum wire with a magnetic field perpendicular to the plane of the wire.
quantum transport in mesoscopic systems in the presence of a magnetic field.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the theory of magnetotunneling in a tilted field is in excellent agreement with experiment.
the semiclassical tunneling theory is in good agreement with experiment, and that the theory is capable of explaining all features of the experimental results.
the semiclassical theory of magnetotunneling through quantum wells in magnetic fields is now in a mature state.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the tunneling current is a sensitive probe of the classical dynamics within the well.
the magnetotunnel resonance spectrum for a tilted field is a rich source of information on the classical dynamics of electrons in the well.
the semiclassical approach to magnetotunneling in tilted fields is a very promising one.
The main takeaway from our work is that
semiclassical tunneling theory can be extended to systems with chaotic dynamics, provided that the tunneling is dominated by periodic orbits.
the magnetotunnel resonance spectrum is determined by the short periodic orbits of the classical system, which can be calculated with high accuracy using the methods presented here.
the semiclassical approach is capable of reproducing the experimental data in a wide parameter regime where perturbation theory is not applicable.
